title: Swapping a Work Shift
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: Colleagues negotiate a shift change around a family commitment.

transcript.text: I found out this morning that the family meal is Thursday, not Friday. I am due to close the shop that evening, so I need someone to swap. I do not want to leave the closing duties uncovered.
I could take Thursday if you cover my Saturday morning. I promised to help a friend move, but they now need me after lunch, so morning is free.
That works. I can do Saturday morning, but cannot stay late because I have an early appointment Sunday.
No problem. I will update the rota once the manager confirms it. We should check the new version in case another shift has moved.

questions.prompt: Why does Colleague A need to change shifts?
options: The shop is closed on Friday.
A family meal has been moved to Thursday.
They have been assigned extra training.
questions.explanation: They explain that the family meal is now on Thursday, when they are due to close.

questions.prompt: What will Colleague A do in return?
options: Move the family meal to Friday
Ask the manager for a different job
questions.explanation: They agree to cover the other colleague’s Saturday morning shift.

questions.prompt: Why can Colleague A not stay late on Saturday?
options: They have an early appointment the next day.
They need to help with a move after lunch.
They are scheduled to close the shop.
questions.explanation: They mention an early appointment on Sunday as the reason.

questions.prompt: What do they plan to check after the change?
options: Whether the shop will open Sunday
Whether the family meal is still happening
Whether another shift has also moved
Whether the friend has finished moving
questions.explanation: They agree to check the updated rota in case any other shift has changed.
